items.title: Censorship, arrests, internet shutdown, PR campaign: How Arunachal is trying to control the Siang dam narrative
items.summary: After protests in Arunachal Pradesh against the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) turned violent on October 23, the state has unleashed a massive crackdown on the movement. The response has included the use of force by armed forces and law enforcement agencies, internet shutdowns, a paid PR campaign, censorship of social media content, and action against journalists and lawyers. A 12-hour Arunachal bandh was called by local bodies and youth groups, including the Siang Indigenous Farmers Forum (SIFF), Adi Baane Kebang United and the Adi Galo Welfare Society, on October 23. The bandh was followed by large-scale arson in Pasighat, East Siang district, targeting an office of the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC), a police station, and the homes of two MLAs and the BJP’s state president. The proposed SUMP, with an estimated capacity of 11,200 megawatts, is planned on the Siang River across the Upper Siang and Siang districts. First proposed in 2008-09 by the UPA government, it was initially conceived as two smaller projects, with memorandums of understanding signed in 2013. On September 26, 2017, following a meeting between chief minister Pema Khandu, state delegates and NITI Aayog, the plan was changed to a single 250-metre-high dam, which would be the country’s largest in terms of installed capacity. However, stiff local resistance forced survey teams to withdraw, bringing the project to a temporary standstill. The BJP-led governments at the Centre and in Arunachal Pradesh revived the project in 2020, following reports of China’s plan to build a dam on the Yarlung Tsangpo River, known as the Siang in India. In April 2022, the Centre directed the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC) to conduct a pre-feasibility survey to assess the project’s technical, economic, social and environmental viability. The exercise involves geological investigations, including drilling, and identifying villages that may require relocation. Chief minister Pema Khandu and other state representatives have maintained that the survey does not amount to a decision to build the dam. NHPC has said that preliminary topographical, geological and geophysical work is complete, but core drilling to assess rock characteristics remains on hold because of local opposition. items.title: Our dignity is at stake: Supreme Court directs Centre to bring back child taken from its custody to Russia
items.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the Central government to take urgent steps to bring a child back to India after he was taken to Russia by his Russian mother despite the child having been placed in the Court's custody earlier [ Viktoriia Basu v. State of West Bengal ]. In an order passed on November 3, a Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu took serious exception to the conduct of the child's mother, Russian national Viktoriia Basu, who allegedly left India through Nepal with her young son and travelled to Russia. The Bench said that the Court's dignity was at stake and that the mother could not be allowed to take advantage of the leniency shown to her during the proceedings. “We are not going to leave this. Our dignity is at stake. After we had taken the child into our custody, the mother, with the help of the Russian Embassy, went away through Nepal. We feel the Russian Federation is aware of it. You (Centre) have to throw all your weight behind this,” the Court orally remarked. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu The matter arose out of a custody dispute between Viktoriia Basu and her estranged husband, Saikat Basu, over their 6-year-old son. She alleged that she had been deprived of access to him following differences with her husband. The Supreme Court subsequently passed several interim orders to facilitate access between the parents and ensure that they could share the child's custody. The couple was initially provided separate accommodation at Banga Bhawan in Delhi and was also referred to mediation in an attempt to resolve their differences. On May 22, 2025, the Court formalised a shared custody arrangement under which the child was to remain in the mother's exclusive custody for three days a week and with the father for the remaining four days. However, on July 7, 2025, the father informed the Court that the mother and child were missing. An investigation by Delhi Police subsequently revealed that Viktoriia had travelled from Delhi to Narkatiaganj in Bihar, entered Nepal and eventually reached Russia through Sharjah in the United Arab Emirates. items.summary: The Delhi High Court has put in abeyance its order directing initiation of criminal proceedings against six former and serving Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) officers [Ashok Kumar Aggarwal v. Sushil Dewan & Ors] . On October 6, Justice Madhu Jain had ordered action against the CBI officials for allegedly making false statements before a court about correspondence with the government while challenging the discharge of a former Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer in a case. The Court had allowed IRS officer Ashok Kumar Aggarwal's plea and directed the Special Judge (CBI) to file a written complaint against Sushil Dewan, Vineet Vinayak, Amit Kumar, Raman Tyagi, Prem Kumar Gautam and Md Azad. The applicants, supported by the CBI, argued that the judgment was passed without hearing them. Only Dewan was a party to the appeal. He claimed he was served on a wrong email ID. items.title: Karnataka High Court quashes BJP defamation case against Congress leaders over ‘40% commission’ ads
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Wednesday quashed the criminal defamation case filed by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) against the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC), Chief Minister DK Shivakumar and former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah over the publication of advertisements accusing the previous BJP government of corruption [Siddaramaiah & others v. BJP]. Justice M Nagaprasanna allowed the petitions filed by the Congress leaders seeking quashing of the criminal proceedings. Justice M Nagaprasanna The case was registered against KPCC, Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Shivakumar and Siddaramaiah over allegations that they were responsible for publishing newspaper advertisements containing derogatory allegations against the BJP-led State government, which was in power between 2019 and 2023 under former Chief Minister Basavaraj Bommai. The advertisements had described the then BJP government as a “40 per cent commission sarkar” , alleging that commissions were being charged in public procurement, allotment of contract works and supply of COVID-19-related materials, among other activities. The advertisements also alleged that the BJP government had looted ₹1,500 crore from the people of Karnataka through corrupt practices. Further, they accused the government of introducing a system of “score cards” and “rate cards” for securing government posts, allegedly referring to bribes paid for appointments. Similar allegations were also made by Rahul Gandhi during a public speech, according to the complaint. The BJP had filed a private complaint in May 2023 against the Congress party, its Karnataka unit and the Congress leaders. A trial court subsequently ordered the registration of criminal defamation proceedings in 2024. The KPCC, Shivakumar and Siddaramaiah approached the High Court seeking to quash the case, contending that the complaint had been filed with the intention of harassing them. The petitioners argued that the advertisements contained allegations of corruption against the then Chief Minister and members of the BJP Cabinet, rather than against the BJP as a political party. They questioned the BJP's legal standing to initiate criminal defamation proceedings, contending that the party was not the person or entity directly aggrieved by the alleged defamatory statements. items.summary: Journalist Anjana Om Kashyap and popular educator Faisal Khan, popularly known as Khan Sir, have resolved their dispute over allegedly defamatory comments made against the news anchor, the Delhi High Court was informed on Wednesday. Justice Tushar Rao Gedela had previously r eferred the parties to mediation and appointed Senior advocate Rajshekhar Rao as the mediator. The Court today lauded Rao for reaching a settlement in the case. “You have done something which was almost impossible. As I said, these things should not come to Court,” Justice Gedela said. A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi issued notice on the appeal filed by Dikshitars challenging the High Court’s October 30 judgment. Therefore, it directed a five-member board to take immediate charge of the administration “till the ill is cured”. The board would comprise two retired High Court judges, a retired IAS officer, the secretary of the Podhu Dikshitars and the State’s Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Secretary, the Court directed. The board was also empowered to regulate darshan, oversee temple finances and recover temple properties. The High Court left daily rituals and periodic festivals to the Dikshitars. items.title: Purchasable FAR destroying Gurugram, Noida: P&H High Court moots stay in Haryana
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Wednesday warned that it will stop implementation of the purchasable Floor Area Ratio (FAR) for constructions in Haryana, observing that it was leading to destruction of urban landscape in cities like Gurugram and Noida. Purchasable FAR is the extra floor area that a developer or property owner in Haryana can build by paying an additional fee to the government, over and above the normal FAR permitted under building regulations. A bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Rohit Kapoor said purchasable FAR destroys the purpose of having a building code. "We have very strong reservations with this purchasable concept. This entire purchasable concept is nothing but a way of distorting and destroying entire building code," the bench stated. The Court said Chandigarh has remained a liveable city only because it does not have the concept of purchasable FIR. It added that cities like Gurgaon and Noida are being destroyed because of purchasable FAR. "What is not permitted otherwise under the building bye-laws is being allowed in the form of one policy or other," the bench said. Hence, it said it is mooting a stay on purchasable FAR and will allow constructions only as per the original building norms. "The moment you go above in the name of purchasable FAR, it is absolute corruption and nothing else," the bench added. Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor The Court further said every city was being destroyed in this fashion. It also flagged the lack of parking, stating a residential unit now has 3-4 cars. "So all your roads are blocked. All your urban townships are being converted into slums," it added The Court further said that unplanned constructions are leading to road rage and parking issues. "We do not want these constructions to come up in the manner that it results in generation of distrust between the neighbours and continuous fight and complete collapse of the urban township itself," it said. The Court said there needs to be a conscious application of mind by authorities to ensure availability of facilities like parking. The Court made these observations while hearing a batch of petitions related to stilt + 4 floor policy in Haryana for residential plots. items.title: Supreme Court seeks response from Centre, ECI on plea challenging blanket immunity for CEC, Election Commissioners
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday sought a response from the Central government and the Election Commission of India (ECI) to a plea challenging a legal provision that protects the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and other Election Commissioners (EC) from any legal action for any act done in the course of their duties. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice on a petition filed by activist and lawyer, Arun Kumar Agrawal. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana The plea challenges the constitutional validity of Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023. This provision extends lifelong protection to the CEC and EC from civil or criminal proceedings for acts done in the discharge of their official duties. The plea points out that similar protection to other constitutional functionaries for actions done in the course of their duties usually extends only to acts done or intended to be done in good faith. The petition recounts that such a balanced approach was also adopted initially when it came to Election Commissioners, before Section 16 was introduced through the 2023 Act. "Despite the absence of such blanket immunity, the Election Commission of India has successfully conducted elections over several decades. This shows that the Commission can function effectively without granting its members blanket immunity from legal proceedings," the plea adds. However, under Section 16, the CEC and ECs have been granted blanket immunity without any exception. Such an approach unconstitutional, disproportionate and liable to be struck down, the petitioner has contended. "The objective of protecting Election Commissioners from vexatious proceedings can be achieved through less restrictive measures, such as safeguards against frivolous complaints and prior judicial scrutiny. Granting blanket immunity is therefore excessive and goes beyond what is necessary to protect the independence of the Election Commission. The said section takes away every civil and criminal remedy against the CEC and ECs for their acts. items.title: Unlikely that 'Pakistan Zindabad' slogan will be raised at BJP rally: Karnataka HC quashes case against participant
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently quashed criminal proceedings against a man accused of raising the slogan ‘Pakistan Zindabad’ during a protest organised by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) [ DS Ravi Kumar v. State of Karntaka ]. In the October 28 ruling, Justice V Srishananda observed that it was unlikely for participants in a BJP-organised demonstration to deliberately raise such a slogan. “At the outset, in a demonstration organized by the Bharathiya Janatha Party-a Political Party, it is highly unimaginable that the protesters therein would raise the slogan 'Pakistan Zindabad.'” In this context, the Court also considered the accused man's contention that the slogan 'Pakistan Zindabad' ('long live Pakistan') had been raised accidentally during the demonstration, instead of the intended slogan 'Pakistan Murdabad' ('death to Pakistan'). items.title: Cannot assume a majority community will vote on community or caste lines: Supreme Court on plea over SC/ST reserved seat
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday asked whether keeping assembly constituencies in Uttar Pradesh reserved for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) candidates for decades without rotation would amount to restriction of electoral choice. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a petition challenging the continued reservation of certain assembly constituencies for SC/ST candidates without rotation for several decades. Justice Bagchi observed that there cannot be an assumption that a majority community will vote on community or caste lines. "That proceeds on the idea that a majority community will vote on community or caste lines. They may not vote on community and caste lines. The High Court cannot judicially pronounce on a democratic choice. That is for the voters to decide." He added that the right to vote was not affected merely because a particular constituency was reserved for candidates belonging to a particular community. "Your right to vote is not in issue. Your right to vote cannot be taken away. You can vote for any community. But if you say that you cannot vote for your community, that will not be countenanced as a valid argument. Your right to contest is not restricted to one constituency. You have other non-reserved constituencies from which you can contest," said Justice Bagchi. He further held that voters in a multiparty democracy were expected to vote based on political ideologies rather than the caste or religion of candidates. "In a political democracy, there are multiple political parties having different ideologies. The voters are expected to vote for the party, not for the religion. You may like or dislike a particular political ideology. Who is representing that ideology becomes irrelevant. You vote for that ideology. So that also defeats your argument," Justice Bagchi told the petitioner. The petitioner's counsel submitted that the authorities could at least be directed to consider introducing rotation, as is done in the case of municipal elections. The Court, however, rejected the plea, suggesting that the petitioner could take up the issue with the legislature and the relevant authorities. items.title: Delhi government lawyer grants consent for contempt of court case against CJP's Ratna Singh
items.summary: Delhi government's Additional Standing Counsel (ASC) Amol Sinha has granted consent to initiate criminal contempt of court proceedings against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) legal head Ratna Singh over her social media criticism of a Chief Judicial Magistrate in Saket Courts. Advocate Kausik Chatterjee had sought action against Singh through a representation dated October 14 and a supplementary one dated October 28. In his November 2 response to Chatterjee, Sinha said the posts prima facie attract Section 2(c)(i) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971. The controversy arose from proceedings before Chief Judicial Magistrate Abhinav Pandey of South-East District. Singh had approached the Court seeking an FIR against police personnel who detained her on October 10 while she was trying to join CJP protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. She had also sought release from alleged detention. The Court declined the relief. Singh then posted the following on X: "Judge serving the master. Went for break/meeting 4 times during entire hearing. Order without any application of law," read one of her tweets. In another tweet, she said, “@DelhiPolice is following order from master. Judge is following order from master." ASC Sinha said that Singh's posts imputed extraneous influence to a judge. He said the posts suggested the judge acted on the instructions of an unidentified external authority, without any factual foundation, and were capable of undermining public confidence in the administration of justice.

items.title: Supreme Court declines to entertain plea challenging Rajasthan Cricket Association elections
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday declined to entertain a challenge concerning the internal election disputes, electoral rolls, and administrative wrangles of the Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA), leaving all contested issues to be adjudicated by the Rajasthan High Court [Rajendra Singh vs State of Rajasthan]. A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi , and Justice V Mohana refused to interfere with the ongoing proceedings, underlining that High Courts are constitutional forums fully equipped to resolve such grievances without apex court oversight. "Let us not predict what the High Court will do. Let us not predict what the outcome will be. If the High Court errs, we are there. But let us not handhold the High Court. The High Court knows how to take a decision and what to do," remarked Justice Bagchi during the hearing. The Court was hearing a petition preferred by Rajendra Singh Nandhu, Secretary of the Nagaur District Cricket Association, challenging the manner in which the RCA's electoral process was conducted. The counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted before the Bench that seven district cricket associations had been unilaterally disbanded, disenfranchising them from the electoral process. Multiple appeals filed by the aggrieved district associations remained pending without resolution, it was pointed out. The petitioner contended that an independent Ombudsman was imperative to examine disputes regarding membership eligibility, affiliation, and voting rights prior to concluding the polls. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The Bench observed that whether State cricket associations are strictly governed by the judicial framework mandated under the Justice Lodha Committee reforms or by subsequent statutory enactments passed by the legislature remains an arguable question of law. Taking note of the factual matrix surrounding the polls, the Court observed that the elections had been conducted under the supervision of an administrator appointed by the Rajasthan High Court, who engaged a former State Chief Election Commissioner as the electoral officer. This officer finalised the electoral rolls after disposing of various objections through reasoned, speaking orders. items.title: Not charity, it is your duty! Bombay High Court asks BMC to clamp down on noise pollution from construction sites
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Wednesday urged civic authorities in Mumbai to ensure that no inconvenience is caused to citizens because of noise pollution, particularly from construction sites. A Bench of Chief Justice Mahesh C Tripathi Justice Avait Sethna was hearing a writ petition filed by a Mumbai citizen challenging the violation of noise pollution norms during an ongoing construction part of a building redevelopment project. “We are not stopping the entire work. We are directing authorities that noise pollution should not cross higher limit. This is to be monitored by senior officials, and police in any and every place,” the Court said. Counsel representing the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) assured the Court that the authorities have been issuing stop-work notices in response to noise pollution complaints about construction activities. items.title: Supreme Court upholds reopening of tax assessments against former CJI YK Sabharwal’s sons
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently upheld the reopening of income-tax assessments against businessmen Chetan Sabharwal and Nitin Sabharwal, sons of former Chief Justice of India late YK Sabharwal , over share transactions involving a total consideration of ₹255 crore [ Chetan Sabharwal v. ACIT, New Delhi ]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran dismissed four appeals filed by the brothers challenging a 2019 Delhi High Court judgment that had upheld the Income Tax (IT) Department’s decision to reopen their assessments. The Court held that an investigation report pointing to the alleged overvaluation of shares constituted tangible material on the basis of which the Assessing Officer could form a reason to believe that income chargeable to tax had escaped assessment. "The expression 'reason to believe' in Section 147 of the Act means cause or justification. The Assessing Officer must have tangible material having a rational connection or a live link with the formation of the belief... At the stage of the notice, the only question is whether there was relevant material on which a reasonable person could have formed the requisite belief, and the sufficiency of the reasons is not a justiciable issue," the Court ruled. items.title: CEC protests: Delhi court seeks police report on journalist's plea for sexual assault FIR against ACP
items.summary: A Delhi court on Tuesday sought a report from the Delhi Police on a plea filed by independent journalist Rosy seeking registration of a first information report (FIR) against Delhi Police officer Vivek Bhagat for allegedly sexually assaulting her during the protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. Rosy approached the Court stating that the Delhi Police failed to register the FIR in the case even a month after she made the complaint. Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) Kautuk Bhardwaj directed the police to file a “point-wise” action taken report stating whether Rosy filed any complaint and whether any action has been taken on it. The Court has also asked the police to state whether, because of investigation/ inquiry, any cognisable offence has been made out against ACP Vivek Bhagat and if an offence is made out, whether any FIR has been registered and the status of the investigation. Notably, the Court has also directed the Police to preserve CCTV and bodycam footage. “In light of the submission and considering the urgency, SHO concerned shall ensure that all necessary steps are taken within 03 days from the receipt of this order, regarding the preservation of CCTV footage pertaining to the place of incident as well as any other digital evidence including body camera footage. The compliance report qua preservation of footage shall be filed within a week,” the Court said in its order. The case will be heard next on December 1. Rosy has accused ACP Bhagat of sexually assaulting and manhandling her while she was covering a protest against Kumar near Jantar Mantar on October 3. The Supreme Court restrained the police from taking coercive action against the journalist . Later, Rosy moved the Delhi High Court challenging the FIR and sought a stay on the investigation. items.title: Allahabad High Court orders FIR against woman for falsely accusing brother of raping her daughter
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has directed the police to register a criminal case against a woman for allegedly getting a false rape case registered against her brother by using her own daughter. Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal took note of the victim's statement before the trial court that her uncle had merely scolded her for use of a mobile phone. "From a perusal of the statements of P.W.-1 and P.W.-2, it is clear that P.W.-2 (first informant) has lodged a false case against the applicant, and this fact has been admitted by her in her statement before the trial court. Therefore, the Senior Superintendent of Police, Meerut, is directed to register an F.I.R. against P.W.-2 (first informant) for lodging a false case against the applicant, as per Section 22 of the POCSO Act," the Court directed. The Court passed the order on October 28 while granting bail to the accused who has been booked by Meerut police under various provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal The prosecution alleged that the minor's maternal uncle had repeatedly raped her. However, during the trial, both the victim and her mother failed to support the prosecution case and were declared hostile. These facts were brought to the High Court's attention during the hearing of the accused's bail application. Counsel for the accused submitted that, in her testimony before the trial court, the minor girl had stated that her uncle had merely scolded her for mobile phone usage, which prompted her to make the false allegation against him. The Court also took note of the victim's mother's (the complainant) testimony before the trial court. She had stated that she lodged the FIR under pressure from a neighbour, adding that her daughter had never told her about any sexual assault and that the police had incorrectly recorded her statement. Seeking bail, the Court was also told the accused has been languishing in jail since long. The State opposed the bail plea but could not dispute the facts on record. items.title: PIL in Delhi High Court seeks action against police officers for threats to use AK-47 against lawyers
items.summary: A lawyer has filed a public interest litigation (PIL) petition before the Delhi High Court alleging threats, intimidation and public vilification of lawyers by serving Delhi Police personnel. The petition, filed by Karan Bir Singh, has sought safeguards for lawyers. The plea comes in the backdrop of the November 2 police protest led by Assistant Commissioner of Police Manasvi Vashishta against lawyers. As per the plea, one policeman issued a public threat that an AK-47 rifle would be used against advocates. “The Petitioner submits that the reported suspension of Respondent No. 4 [ACP Vashishta] does not adequately address the wider constitutional issues arising from the alleged conduct, particularly the continued circulation of threatening videos, the absence of appropriate action against other concerned officials and the need to safeguard advocates from unlawful intimidation while discharging their professional duties,” the plea filed through advocate Vikrant Dabas states. items.title: Both Supreme Court and Manusmriti hold maintenance of wife to be pious obligation of husband: Allahabad High Court
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently directed that enhanced maintenance be paid to a woman from her husband's salary, while referring to a Supreme Court ruling and a verse from the Manusmriti [Pinki Verma And Another v State of UP and Another] Justice Praveen Kumar Giri observed that both the top court and Manusmriti have held maintenance of wife to be a husband's pious obligation. "This Court observes that not only legal but a pious obligation is upon the husband to maintain his chaste wife, minor children and parents, if they are financially unable to maintain themselves. The same has also been observed in paragraph 10 of judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Anju Garg and another vs. Deepak Kumar Garg, 2022 INSC 1033 : 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1314 , Section 125 Cr.P.C./144 BNSS as well as in Chapter XI Verse 10 (Ekadasha Adhyaya Shlok 10) of the Manusmriti," the Court said. The Court reproduced the Supreme Court findings, the legal provisions and the verse of Manusmriti in its order. Justice Praveen Kumar Giri The Court was dealing with a woman's petition seeking directions for payment of ₹40,000 per month from her husband. A family court earlier directed payment of maintenance of ₹19,000 to her. It was argued that the payment of maintenance to her was not in accordance with the Supreme Court's ruling that 25 percent of the husband's salary would be just and proper towards maintenance. Her husband, who is working as a window operator in Indian Bank, agreed to the deduction. Accordingly, the Court directed deduction of 25 percent of his gross salary, after excluding the amount deducted towards income tax, as maintenance amount from his salary account and for crediting the same to the verified bank account of wife. "The concerned trial court i.e. Principal Judge, Family Court, Kanpur Nagar is also directed to pass an order directing the concerned higher authority of the Indian Bank, District Unnao to deduct 25% of his gross salary, after excluding the amount deducted towards income tax, as maintenance amount from his salary account and for crediting the same to the verified bank account of revisionist no.1/wife," the Court ordered. items.title: Jantar Mantar should never have been a protest site; de-notified due to limited capacity: Delhi Police to Supreme Court
items.summary: Jantar Mantar is a public road and should never have been earmarked as a designated protest venue, the Delhi Police told the Supreme Court on Tuesday. In an affidavit filed before the Court by Delhi Police Commissioner (DCP) Anurag Kumar, it was stated that Jantar Mantar was de-notified as a protest site due to its limited capacity to accommodate large footfall, and its proximity to sensitive government institutions and embassies of foreign nations. The decision was taken by Kumar on the unanimous recommendation of a Ministry of Home Affairs committee, it was submitted. He termed the decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as a administrative and executive decision. Further, nobody has the fundamental right to protest at a particular site, the affidavit added. The counter affidavit was filed in response to a petition by advocate Swaty Singh challenging the de-notification. Singh moved the Court contending that the move to de-notify Jantar Mantar violates the fundamental rights to freedom of speech and expression and to assemble peacefully under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) of the Constitution. While the State can regulate these rights in the interest of public order, the petition by Singh stated that such regulation cannot operate as a prohibition or render the exercise of these rights illusory. It further was further argued that the location of a protest site is central to the protests. According to the plea, proximity to the concerned institutions, accessibility to the public and visibility to the intended audience directly affect a protest's effectiveness. In his response, the DCP has claimed that Jantar Mantar has a capacity of 1,500 persons and the protests by Cockroach Janta Party in July far exceeded the capacity. Further, there are around 78 embassies and missions and 99 Central government offices, with a daily footfall of 1,46,040, within 3 to 4 km, besides about 64,500 residents in nearby housing areas. For August 1 to 27, there were about 250 distress calls, 109 theft FIRs, 10 vehicle theft FIRs, 254 property-loss claims, 23 FIRs for public order violations, rioting and defacement, and 14 cases under the Delhi Police Act, it was pointed. In light of the above, it was found fit to de-notify the site. "In the era of digital technology and widespread use of social media, the geographical proximity of a protest site to the seat of the Government has ceased to be relevant and has become redundant," the affidavit said. items.title: Calling wife ‘stupid’, ‘useless’ not cruelty: Supreme Court quashes case against husband after her suicide
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday quashed a dowry death and cruelty case against a man whose wife died by suicide. The Court observed that allegations that he called her “stupid” and “useless”, even if true, do not constitute cruelty or criminal intimidation. A Bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and Manmohan set aside a Bombay High Court order refusing to quash the proceedings against the husband, finding no material establishing a nexus between the alleged harassment and his wife’s death. “The allegation that the appellant used to call the deceased ‘stupid’ and ‘useless,’ even if accepted prima facie, cannot to any extent qualify as an offence of cruelty or criminal intimidation. At best, it reflects on the temperament of the husband, but it cannot be given a criminal colour so grave as to become the reason for the suicide of his wife,” the Court observed. Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice Manmohan The Bench also stressed that general allegations of harassment, without details of specific offending acts, were insufficient to continue criminal proceedings. The couple married in January 2021 and moved to Toronto, Canada in February 2022. The wife died by suicide in June 2023. Her suicide note referred to difficulties with her studies and finding employment as well as feelings of being “stupid” and “useless”. Her father lodged a complaint in Maharashtra in June 2023, alleging that the husband and his family demanded gold and money as dowry and subjected his daughter to physical and mental harassment. A first information report (FIR) was registered invoking Sections 304B (dowry death), 323 (voluntarily causing hurt), 498A (cruelty by a husband or his relatives) and 504 (intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of peace), read with Section 34 (common intention), of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). items.title: NEET to move from percentile-based to rank-based system: Centre tells Supreme Court
items.summary: A 12-member expert committee constituted to review the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test for Postgraduates (NEET-PG) admission system has proposed replacing the existing percentile-based qualifying system with a rank-based merit system. In a report filed before the Supreme Court, the committee said that the National Medical Commission (NMC) had granted in-principle approval to the proposal for both NEET-PG and the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test for Super Speciality (NEET-SS). A draft regulation is expected to be issued shortly for stakeholder consultation. The committee also suggested several measures to address the recurring problem of vacant postgraduate medical seats, including reducing fees for non-clinical courses and exempting candidates taking pre-clinical and para-clinical seats from service bonds. The report was submitted pursuant to the Supreme Court’s directions to the Union government to conduct a comprehensive audit of the existing NEET admission system, identify gaps and recommend practical solutions. The issue arose from the Union Health Ministry’s decision to drastically reduce the qualifying cut-off percentiles for NEET-PG 2025. Under the revised criteria, the qualifying score for the general category was reduced from 276 to 103, while that for the SC/ST/OBC categories was brought down from 235 to minus 40. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday initiated contempt of court proceedings against the Municipal Commissioner of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) for failing to comply with its earlier directions to remove encroachments from land earmarked for a Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) bus stand. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued a show cause notice to the Municipal Commissioner, seeking a response as to why contempt action should not be initiated. The Court also dismissed the commissioner's plea for more time to comply, slapping ₹5 lakh costs and ordering a halt to salary payments. Additionally, CJI Kant questioned whether municipal officers were deliberately avoiding compliance with the Supreme Court's directions. "Does it not show that your officers are colluding? We will send him to jail and then he will understand the sanctity of the Supreme Court order. Is he obliging us?" said CJI Kant . items.title: Bombay High Court orders equal compensation for landlord and tenant in Siddhivinayak land acquisition
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Tuesday ordered an equal 50:50 split of ₹10.94 crore land acquisition compensation between the landowners and their long-term tenant, Sadanand Garage, for a Prabhadevi property acquired for Mumbai’s Shree Siddhivinayak Ganapati Temple Trust [Special Land Acquisition Officer v. Kapu A Shetty & Anr] Justice Amit Borkar determined the market value of the 642.98 square-metre plot at ₹1,70,200 per square metre as of September 19, 2002. The State had acquired the land to construct a waiting hall and Bhakti Niwas for visiting devotees. Justice Amit Borkar The court rejected the Special Land Acquisition Officer’s reliance on ready reckoner rates. It reiterated that such rates lack statutory foundation for determining open-market value under Section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. The judge instead evaluated genuine registered transactions of comparable properties in the immediate vicinity. The final compensation was fixed at ₹10.94 crores for the land, alongside ₹3.85 lakh awarded exclusively to the owners for existing structures and trees. A dispute arose regarding the division of this sum. The landowners demanded the entire award, whereas Sadanand Garage claimed a 75 percent share citing continuous occupation since 1971. The Court found that while the garage proved a valid tenancy and business occupation, it failed to demonstrate exclusive title or perpetual lease over the entire open plot. Justice Borkar observed that valuation must reflect the actual encumbrance. “The owner cannot claim the value of the property as though the land was vacant and was available in his own possession when a tenant was occupying it,” the judge held. He concluded that equal apportionment of the amount was fair given the facts of the case. “The owners had substantial ownership rights, though those rights were subject to the established tenancy and occupation rights of the Garage,” the judge held. items.title: Wife's LinkedIn profile not proof of income, can't be ground to deny maintenance: Bengaluru court
items.summary: A Bengaluru court has held that photographs and social media profiles, including LinkedIn and Facebook, cannot by themselves establish that a woman has sufficient income to maintain herself and her child and consequently disentitle her from maintenance. Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge Mohan Prabhu made the observation while rejecting a husband's contention that his wife was employed at a private company and therefore did not require financial support. " The trial court records show that while addressing the arguments, the learned counsel for the respondent has produced certain photographs, LinkedIn profile and Facebook profile photos, and contended that the petitioner is working " the Court noted. The Court, however, found that the husband had failed to establish his wife's actual earnings. " The learned magistrate rightly held that the documents produced by the learned counsel for the respondent at the time of arguments cannot be relied, " the Court observed. It further held that even if the woman had secured employment, it would not necessarily establish that she earned enough to maintain herself and her minor child. items.title: Kerala HC sets aside single-judge order permitting suspended Sanskrit University students to write exams

The bench of Justices Anil K Narendran and Muralee Krishna S passed the ruling on an appeal filed by the university against the single-judge's October 30 interim order. items.title: Shopkeepers need not provide free carry bags to customers: Uttarakhand Consumer Commission
items.summary: The Uttarakhand State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has held that shopkeepers are under no legal obligation to provide free carry bags to customers, particularly when customers voluntarily agree to purchase them after being informed of the charges. [Ramesh Singh Vs Vishal Mega Mart] A Bench of President Kumkum Rani and Member BS Manral dismissed an appeal filed by a customer against Vishal Mega Mart over a charge of ₹18 for a carry bag. The Commission held that charging for a carry bag would not constitute an unfair trade practice when customers were informed of its price and were free to decline the purchase. " It is also well settled that the shopkeeper is under no obligation to supply carry bags and that too, without any cost and there is no law which mandates providing free carry bag to the customer ," the Commission observed in its order of October 30. items.title: You cannot occupy protest site for all time; what about livelihood of daily wagers? Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said that protestors cannot perpetually occupy a protest site, adding that such sites can be occupied only for a specified period to allow other groups to use them. A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a batch of petitions arising from the October protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. "You cannot occupy a site for all times to come. There are other protesters. Where will the farmers go? Where will the workers go? Where will the trade unions go? Where will the homeless go? Everybody has a right to protest," CJI Kant said. The Court also referred to the losses suffered by daily wagers because of the protests. "There are conflicting claims. The right to protest is also a constitutionally recognised right, as is the right to trade and carry on business. We are not talking about trade merely in terms of commercial establishments. We are talking about the source of livelihood of a daily-wage worker. Where does that person go for their daily bread?," CJI Kant said. CJI Kant further referred to the competing claims among protestors intending to highlight varying causes. "You must also find out why further time is not being granted. There may be another request for another protest. There may be one site or two, but everybody has a right to protest...You cannot exclude other people merely because you have occupied the site. You cannot say that because you have occupied it, you will not allow others," he said. items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court recently quashed a criminal case against a journalist accused of promoting enmity through a news report on an incident of violence during a Ganesh Visarjan procession in 2025 [Uvesh Khan @ Uvesh Reporter vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh] Justice Himanshu Joshi said that mere reporting of an incident involving violence does not constitute the offence of promoting enmity or disharmony between different groups under Section 196(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). items.title: Account blocking by LinkedIn to be challenged through civil suit, not writ petition: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that a writ petition is not maintainable against LinkedIn or its resident grievance officer over their decision to block/restrict an account [Mayank Jain v. Union of India & Ors] . Justice Amit Mahajan held that the threshold for a private entity to be amenable to writ jurisdiction is that it must undertake functions that are fundamentally governmental in nature or are performed by virtue of power vested by law. The Court underscored that LinkedIn does not perform a public function or public duty. “While the platform provided by Respondent No. 2 [LinkedIn] plays a significant role in disseminating information and shaping public opinion, its primary function is to provide a platform for expression, with public discourse being a consequence of its operations rather than a public duty. Its operations remain private in nature, and no governmental mandate delegates any traditional State function to it. Respondent No. 2 is neither obligated to provide such a platform in discharge of a public duty nor legally compelled to offer its services, which are voluntary and user-driven,” the Court observed. It added that a civil suit is a more appropriate remedy in such a case. After hearing the case, the High Court noted that Jain had already approached the Grievance Appellate Committee under the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021. It concluded that LinkedIn or its resident grievance officer cannot be subjected to the writ jurisdiction. Advocate Anjali appeared for the petitioner. items.title: Jet Airways liquidator moves NCLAT for $92.13 million refund from Boeing over undelivered aircraft
items.summary: Jet Airways’ liquidator has moved the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) seeking a refund of $92.13 million paid to Boeing as advances for aircraft that were never delivered [Jet Airways Vs Boeing]. A bench of Justice Mohammad Faiz Alam Khan and Technical Member Naresh Salecha issued notice to Boeing after observing that the appeal required consideration. Boeing’s counsel accepted notice and was granted two weeks to file a reply. The liquidator was given one week thereafter to file a rejoinder. The matter will be heard next in the first week of December. The appeal challenged a September 11 order of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) dismissing liquidator Satish Kumar Gupta’s application seeking recovery of $92,129,387 from Boeing. During the hearing at NCLAT today, the counsel for the liquidator submitted that Boeing had forfeited Jet Airways’ advance payments and then lodged a claim for the unpaid balance during the airline’s corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP). The counsel clarified that the appeal concerned recovery of the advances. The liquidator sought notice without pressing for interim relief. The dispute arose from two purchase agreements executed in 2013 for Boeing 737-8 and 787-9 aircraft. Jet Airways made advance and pre-delivery payments but subsequently failed to meet further payment obligations amid financial difficulties. Boeing issued a suspension notice in May 2019 and a termination notice in December 2020. No aircraft were delivered under the agreements. Before the NCLT, the liquidator argued that the advances formed part of Jet Airways’ liquidation estate and ought to be returned. He contended that Boeing had not established any contractual or legal entitlement to retain them. Boeing maintained that the advances had already been deducted while calculating its outstanding claim against the airline. It argued that the liquidator could not recover amounts already credited against a larger claim admitted during insolvency and subsequently recognised in liquidation. items.title: Private CCTV cameras can't be positioned to invade neighbour’s privacy: Allahabad High Court
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently observed that no one can install or position a private CCTV camera in a manner that interferes with the privacy of their neighbour [ Yogendra Maurya v. State of UP ]. A Division Bench comprising Justice Ajit Kumar and Justice Garima Prashad observed that such surveillance of a neighbour’s residential premises would amount to an infringement of privacy. “No private CCTV camera can be installed and positioned in such a manner as to interfere with the privacy of a neighbour," the Court said. Justice Ajit Kumar and Justice Garima Prashad The High Court was hearing a writ petition filed by one Yogendra Maurya, who alleged that his neighbour had positioned a CCTV camera in a manner that exposed the entry and exit points of his house and interfered with the privacy of persons visiting or leaving the premise. He contended that this amounted to a violation of his privacy. The Court noted that no private CCTV camera can be installed and positioned in such a manner as to interfere with the privacy of a neighbour. However, did not issue any direction for the removal of the CCTV camera. Instead, it closed the writ petition by directing the petitioner to file an appropriate application before the concerned District Magistrate for relief. The Bench further directed that if such an application for the CCTV camera's removal is filed, the District Magistrate shall consider and decide the same within one month. Advocate Akhilesh Singh Yadav appeared on behalf of the petitioner. items.title: MP High Court sets aside ex parte order after lawyer fails to appear, inform client of hearings
items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court recently held that litigants cannot be made to suffer for the negligence of their advocates, while setting aside an ex-parte order passed by a trial court against a woman who was allegedly kept in the dark by her lawyer about the progress of a civil suit [ Ku. Jyoti Singh vs Chetan Lashkari ]. Expressing shock over advocates failing to discharge duties with sincerity, the Court's also directed the State Bar Council to examine and initiate possible suo motu disciplinary action against the lawyer whose negligence and misleading updates led to his client being proceeded against ex parte. Justice Sandeep N Bhatt passed the order on a plea filed by the litigant (petitioner) to set aside an ex parte order passed by a trial court against her that had closed her right to contest a civil suit. The petitioner referred to WhatsApp chats indicating that she had diligently followed up on the progress of her case with her counsel. However, after the lawyer failed to appear before the trial court, the petitioner's right to contest the civil suit was closed through the ex-parte order (order passed in the absence of a party or their counsel). The Court on October 30 set aside the ex parte trial court order and restored the petitioner's right to contest the civil suit. It held that an innocent party who acts diligently cannot be made to suffer for the inaction or omissions of their counsel. "I am of the view that the petitioner should not suffer for the mistake committed by the counsel and therefore, the Court has to exercise jurisdiction under Article 227 of the Constitution of India to prevent the miscarriage of the justice," the Bench observed. items.title: File a petition: Delhi High Court refuses suo motu case against ACP Manasvi Vashishta for threats to lawyers
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Tuesday refused to take suo motu cognisance of alleged threats made by Delhi Police officer Manasvi Vashishta against lawyers. Vashishta was seen on video making remarks against lawyers and warning "goon in black coats" of serious repercussions. A Division Bench of acting Chief Justice (ACJ) Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma asked lawyers to file a formal petition and assured that the issue will be looked into. A group of lawyers had mentioned the matter before the acting Chief Justice. Lawyers told the Court that remarks like the use of AK47 and "Kaale coat ke Gunde (goons in black coats)" were used against lawyers. "You [Acting Chief Justice] are our chief. If you take suo motu cognisance we will be assured," the lawyers told the Bench today. However, the Court asked the lawyers to file a formal petition and assured them that the Court will direct its listing and look into it. "You file a formal petition. We will look into it. You give representation, but also file a formal petition," the court told the lawyers. items.title: CJI Surya Kant inaugurates Jharkhand High Court’s data centre, stresses need to protect judicial records
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Monday inaugurated the Jharkhand High Court’s data centre. Speaking at the event, he stressed the need to protect sensitive judicial records against unauthorised access, loss and disruption. “Judicial records contain sensitive information and must be protected against unauthorised access, loss and disruption. Cybersecurity, reliable backup arrangements, regular testing and trained technical personnel are essential to maintaining public confidence in digital systems,” he stated. The data centre project represents an investment of approximately ₹25 crore. Its value, the CJI noted, would be measured by improvements in court functioning and the experience of litigants, rather than the equipment installed. The event also marked the launch of the High Court’s new website, an online certified copy application for civil courts across Jharkhand, a personalised cause list and Dragon speech-to-text software. Highlighting their practical benefits, the CJI explained that the online certified copy facility would reduce unnecessary travel and expense for litigants, while the personalised cause list would help advocates locate cases and prepare for hearings. He also stressed the need to carefully verify documents prepared using speech-to-text tools, particularly legal terminology, names and citations. “Speed cannot come at the cost of accuracy, and responsibility for the final text must remain with the concerned human user,” he cautioned. Turning to artificial intelligence, the CJI underlined that technology could support research, documentation and information management but could not replace judicial judgment. He also emphasised that people who lack digital literacy, reliable internet access or the ability to navigate online systems must not be left behind. “Digital services must widen access to justice, not create new barriers to it,” the CJI said. items.summary: The Madras High Court on Monday observed that the police serve the State and not the political party in power, while granting anticipatory bail to a Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) councillor accused of making derogatory remarks against Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) leader Vijay [ D Sudha v. Justice N Ramesh said that an impartial police force was essential to constitutional governance and that the machinery of criminal law could not be deployed merely because political speech offended those holding public office. " An even hand between the ruling party and its opponents is not a courtesy the police extend; it is a condition of their constitutional legitimacy. The police serve the State, which endures, and not the party in government, which changes ," the Court observed. The Court said that it is common knowledge that political discourse is substantially conducted on social media by the IT wings of political parties, and that such content often involves trolling and abuse of rivals. Commenting on the instant case, the Court said that while there is nothing on record to indicate that the police acted on the TVK party's behest, it must also be mindful of how its actions may be interpreted by a citizen. It recounted that he was released the same day after the Chief Minister intervened. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday sought responses from the Allahabad High Court administration and Additional District Judge (ADJ) Ashok Bhartendu on a petition filed by a rape survivor seeking Bhartendu's removal as a special POCSO judge in view of a pending rape case against him in Delhi. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi , and Justice V Mohana also said that it would examine the progress of the vigilance complaint lodged against Bhartendu. items.title: Delhi High Court quashes CIC order directing HC to provide data under RTI on delayed judgments
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has set aside a Central Information Commission (CIC) order directing the court’s Public Information Officer (PIO) to locate and provide details of cases in which judgments were reserved but pronounced more than two months later [Public Information Officer v PD Gupta] . Justice Amit Mahajan allowed a 2011 petition filed by the PIO of the High Court against the CIC’s May 26, 2011, order. The Court observed that while timely delivery of judgments is a matter of public concern, the consideration of public interest arises only when the information exists. “The same cannot be used to compel a public authority to create information which is not held by it,” the Court said. In the present case such information was not maintained by the High Court, and in order to provide the information sought, the public authority would have to examine records of all cases heard by a particular judge and prepare a fresh compilation, the Court noted. Justice Amit Mahajan, Delhi High Court The case arose from a Right to Information (RTI) application filed in 2009 by former judicial officer PD Gupta. He sought details of cases heard by then Delhi High Court Justice AK Sikri, either sitting as a single-judge or as part of a Division Bench, where judgments were delivered more than two months after arguments concluded. The PIO replied that no such data was specifically maintained or compiled. However, the CIC directed the PIO to locate monthly reports furnished by court masters regarding reserved judgments and provide the information for two years preceding the RTI application. Justice Mahajan noted that monthly lists regarding reserved judgments were sent in sealed covers to the Chief Justice to enable administrative action on delayed matters. The Court added that these lists were not required to be preserved or compiled judge-wise. Providing the information sought would require the Court to examine records of all cases heard by a particular judge and prepare a fresh compilation, the Court said. It added that the RTI Act does not oblige a public authority to collect or collate information that is not maintained. “The learned CIC in the impugned order proceeds merely on the premise that the information “should be available” on account of the practice of furnishing such lists to Hon’ble the Chief Justice. items.summary: The Rajasthan High Court full bench on Monday held that writ petitions arising from criminal matters must be registered separately as criminal writ petitions [Ravi Kumar v State Of Rajasthan & Ors.] . A Bench of Chief Justice Sanjay K Agrawal , Justice Sameer Jain and Justice Anuroop Singhi overruled an earlier verdict rendered in this regard by a division bench headed by former acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma. The full bench observed that the July 2026 division bench ruling of the Court had failed to consider Rule 315(1)(h) of the Rajasthan High Court Rules, which requires writ petitions arising from criminal matters to be registered separately. "The aforesaid decision in Jiya failed to consider or give effect to the statutory mandate embodied in Rule 315(1)(h) of the Rajasthan High Court Rules, its ratio, insofar as it prohibits criminal-side registration of such writ applications, is held to be per incuriam, having been rendered in ignorance of, or without due consideration of, a relevant statutory provision," held the full bench. Justice Sanjay K Agrawal, Justice Sameer Jain and Justice Anuroop Singhi The full bench further clarified that the separate classification did not mean that the Constitution recognised a distinct category of criminal writ jurisdiction. Instead, it was a procedural distinction under the High Court Rules to identify writ petitions arising from criminal proceedings and ensure that they were placed before the appropriate Bench. "The classification of a petition as a ‘criminal writ petition’ does not create an independent constitutional jurisdiction; it identifies the procedural character of a writ proceeding arising from a criminal matter and must be understood in conjunction with the constitutional jurisdiction under Article 226 and the applicable High Court Rules," said the Court. The Court directed the registry to reclassify criminal writ petitions that were pending but had been registered under a different name, and place them before the appropriate bench within two weeks. “The criminal writ petitions concerning criminal matters that are pending as on the date of this judgment but have been registered under a different nomenclature, the Registry shall re-register the same as 'Criminal Writ Petition' and shall place the writ petition before the appropriate Bench having the roster. items.title: Kerala: 17-year-old boy murdered after being used as bait to lure another teen
items.summary: The 17-year-old boy murdered in Thiruvananthapuram was allegedly used as bait to lure another teenager whom the accused had planned to kill over a personal dispute, the city police have said. Investigators suspect that the murder was part of a premeditated plan, with the first accused – a 17-year-old boy – discussing the killing days in advance and sharing a photograph of an axe with an 18-year-old girl who is among those arrested. City Police Commissioner Arul RB Krishna said the accused had intended to use the victim, MD Abhiram, to bring his friend to an isolated location in Pangappara. However, when Abhiram did not cooperate, the plan allegedly took a different turn, resulting in his murder. Abhiram, a plus-two student and resident of Sreekaryam, went missing on the night of November 1. His body was found in an isolated area at Pangappara, near Sreekaryam, on the evening of November 2. The police subsequently arrested three persons, a 17-year-old boy (first accused), an 18-year-old girl (third accused) and Umar Muqthar (second accused), who had been detained under the Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (KAAPA). Speaking to the media on Wednesday, November 4, the Commissioner said the first accused had discussed killing the intended target with the girl two to three days before the incident. He had also shared a photograph of an axe with her on WhatsApp, indicating that the attack had been planned. "The boy (Abhiram) was deliberately summoned to that location with a specific intention," the Commissioner said, adding that the police were still investigating whom the accused had originally intended to target. According to the Commissioner, the plan was to use Abhiram to bring another boy, whom the first accused considered an enemy, to the location. However, when Abhiram did not cooperate, the situation escalated and led to his murder. Police suspect a dispute linked to the first accused's previous personal relationship was behind the plan. The accused and Abhiram were not necessarily close friends, but they lived in neighbouring areas and had some mutual acquaintances, the Commissioner said. The police are also examining the role of the 18-year-old girl, who allegedly helped summon Abhiram to the location. items.title: Pro-Kannada group meets Google and other tech firms, urges them to hire more locals
items.summary: The Karnataka Rakshana Vedike (KRV), on November 4, held a meeting with representatives of around 30 IT companies in Bengaluru’s Mahadevapura and submitted memorandums seeking fair employment opportunities for Kannadigas in the state’s IT sector. The pro-Kannada organisation also visited Google’s office in Bengaluru and submitted a memorandum raising the same demand. A KRV delegation met human resources officials of the companies at the Brigade complex and submitted a memorandum to each, outlining the organisation’s concerns over alleged discrimination against local candidates during recruitment. KRV state president TA Narayana Gowda participated in the meeting via a video call and explained the campaign's objectives. The organisation said representatives of all the companies responded positively to its demands and assured the delegation they would consider the concerns raised. The organisation plans to submit a comprehensive report to the state government and seek time-bound action on implementing job reservations. The delegation was led by KRV state vice-president Veerabhadra. Mahadevapura unit president Lohith, KR Puram unit president Manjunath and other office-bearers, including Rama, Lakshmana, Anand and Nagaraj, were also present. The campaign comes days after Chief Minister DK Shivakumar said the government would take action against private companies found to be deliberately sidelining Kannadigas in recruitment. He had also cautioned pro-Kannada organisations against taking the law into their own hands. The issue has revived the debate over reservations for local candidates in the private sector. In 2024, the Karnataka Cabinet approved a Bill proposing reservations for Kannadigas in private industries. items.title: Telangana woman allegedly beheaded by in-laws over land dispute
items.summary: A 28-year-old woman was allegedly beheaded by her in-laws over a property dispute in Telangana’s Mahbubnagar district on Monday, November 2. The accused allegedly attacked her with sharp-edged weapons after dragging her to their house, police said. The victim, K Sunitha, was a native of Obulayyapalli village in Mahbubnagar mandal. She is survived by two daughters, aged five and two. Her husband, K Balaram, reportedly has mental health issues. According to police, Sunitha was on her way to her agricultural field in Chinthal Thanda in Koilkonda mandal on Monday afternoon when her father-in-law, Manikya Naik, and her brothers-in-law, Manya Naik and Pandu Naik, along with Pandu’s wife, Parvathy, allegedly intercepted her. They tied a cloth around her neck and dragged her to their house, where they attacked her with knives and severed her head. Police suspect that the murder was premeditated. Police rushed to the spot after receiving information and shifted the body to the Mahbubnagar Government General Hospital for a postmortem examination. According to The Indian Express, the accused are absconding, and special teams have been formed to nab them. Sunitha married Balaram, a resident of Chinthal Thanda, over a decade ago. The couple frequently quarrelled, reportedly due to Balaram’s mental health issues. About a year ago, village elders intervened to resolve the disputes. As part of the settlement, the village elders registered around 1.5 acres of agricultural land belonging to Balaram in Sunitha’s name to secure her and her daughters’ future. However, the decision reportedly angered Balaram’s elder brothers, Manya Naik and Pandu Naik, who opposed the transfer of the land. Police said that the brothers frequently took Balaram to Hyderabad for treatment and allegedly prevented the couple from living together. Sunitha subsequently moved to her parents’ home in Obulayyapalli. Her parents later persuaded her to return to Chinthal Thanda and built a house for her. She had been living there with her two daughters for the past month. Despite this, her in-laws allegedly continued to pressure her to relinquish the land and leave the village. They also threatened to kill her if she refused, police said. According to reports, the accused suspected Sunitha was in a relationship with another person and feared that she might remarry, potentially transferring the land to her new husband.
